annotation.authors_or_issuer: Defra (UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs); co-chairs George Eustice MP and Professor Simon Pearson
key_provisions_or_claims: Identifies six technology clusters, from optimised production systems and packhouse automation to autonomous selective harvesting.
Autonomous selective harvesting offers high labour savings but is unlikely to be commercially available well before 2030 if left to market forces.
Many systems sit at TRL 5-6 in the 'valley of death', where capital for development is scarce.
Barriers include fragmented knowledge sharing, lack of independent business advice, and limited investment capital.
Recommendations are non-binding and are meant to create an enabling environment for robotics development and adoption.
annotation.summary_en: Defra-led UK government review, co-chaired by the Secretary of State and Prof. Simon Pearson, on accelerating automation and agri-robotics in horticulture to reduce reliance on seasonal migrant labour. It sets out technology clusters, adoption barriers such as the 'valley of death' and knowledge gaps, and non-binding recommendations to government.
